question: Does the pre-linear post-turn correction site (services.py post_turn_alignment) need the same >=90 degree reverse-recovery guard that beta22 applied to the post-linear site?
method: Offline replay of every committed multi-segment real result. No motion, no mower. Read post_turn_alignment.before.aim_error_degrees from each segment.
conclusion: LEAVE UNGUARDED. No recorded run has ever produced a post-turn aim error at or beyond 90 degrees; the worst observed is 18.78 degrees, roughly a fifth of the boundary, and both corrections that ran succeeded. Adding the guard here would be an un-evidenced motion-path change guarding a condition that has never occurred, and it would carry a real cost: at this site a >=90 degree reading is far more likely to indicate a bad VIO offset or a corrupt bearing than a genuine overshoot, because the mower has not yet driven forward on this segment. Failing closed on it would convert a recoverable state into a refused run.
revisit_if: A recorded run produces a post-turn aim error above roughly 45 degrees, i.e. the observed maximum doubles.
max_turn_translation_distance is raised above 0.30, which would let the initial turn carry the mower further past a short waypoint.
Waypoint legs shorter than about 0.30 m are adopted, where 0.207 m of turn drift is a large fraction of the leg.
caveats: Ten records from eight runs, all on the LUBA at one site, all with max_turn_translation_distance at 0.25 or 0.30.
This is an offline replay of committed evidence, not a hardware test.
The post-linear guard shipped in beta22 is unaffected by this finding and stays in place.
